claim: COLD was recently shown to resolve up to four binding sites on a single protein.
source: Cryogenic optical localization in three dimensions (COLD) was recently shown to resolve up to four binding sites on a single protein.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract without specific data or citation in this sentence, but is a claim about prior work.

claim: COLD relies on intensity fluctuations that result from the blinking behavior of fluorophores.
source: However, because COLD relies on intensity fluctuations that result from the blinking behavior of fluorophores, it is limited to cases where individual emitters show different brightness.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the COLD method based on established knowledge of the technique.

claim: COLD is limited to cases where individual emitters show different brightness.
source: However, because COLD relies on intensity fluctuations that result from the blinking behavior of fluorophores, it is limited to cases where individual emitters show different brightness.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the COLD method based on its operational principle.

claim: The brightness limitation of COLD significantly lowers the measurement yield.
source: This significantly lowers the measurement yield.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the brightness limitation.

claim: polarCOLD employs partial labeling combined with polarization encoding to identify single fluorophores during stochastic blinking.
source: To extend the number of resolved sites as well as the measurement yield, we employ partial labeling and combine it with polarization encoding in order to identify single fluorophores during their stochastic blinking.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach of the current study.

claim: polarCOLD uses a particle classification scheme to identify and resolve heterogenous subsets.
source: We then use a particle classification scheme to identify and resolve heterogenous subsets and combine them to reconstruct the three-dimensional arrangement of large molecular complexes.
evidence: This describes the analytical approach used in the study.

claim: polarCOLD resolves the trimer arrangement of PCNA with Angstrom resolution.
source: We showcase this method (polarCOLD) by resolving the trimer arrangement of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) and six different sites of the hexamer protein Caseinolytic Peptidase B (ClpB) of Thermus thermophilus in its quaternary structure, both with Angstrom resolution.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: polarCOLD resolves six different sites of the hexamer protein ClpB with Angstrom resolution.
source: We showcase this method (polarCOLD) by resolving the trimer arrangement of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) and six different sites of the hexamer protein Caseinolytic Peptidase B (ClpB) of Thermus thermophilus in its quaternary structure, both with Angstrom resolution.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The combination of polarCOLD and single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy promises to provide crucial insight into intrinsic heterogeneities of biomolecular structures.
source: The combination of polarCOLD and single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) promises to provide crucial insight into intrinsic heterogeneities of biomolecular structures.
evidence: This is a prospective claim about the potential application of the method.

claim: polarCOLD is fully compatible with fluorescent protein labeling.
source: Furthermore, our approach is fully compatible with fluorescent protein labeling and can, thus, be used in a wide range of studies in cell and membrane biology.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the method.

claim: Proteins and their assemblies govern every aspect of cellular physiology in both healthy and disease states.
source: Proteins and their various assemblies are among the main constituents of all living systems and govern every aspect of cellular physiology in both healthy and disease states (Nelson, 2017; Mavroidis et al., 2004; Schliwa and Woehlke, 2003; Alberts, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Understanding the spatial arrangements and heterogeneous configurations of proteins is crucial for elucidating their molecular mechanisms.
source: A full understanding of their spatial arrangements and associated heterogeneous configurations is crucial for elucidating their molecular mechanisms, helps guide the engineering of new proteins, and is a great asset for drug discovery (Renaud et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: X-ray crystallography has been used to gain insight into protein structure and function.
source: Indeed, since the pioneering work of Perutz on protein crystals (Fersht, 2008), a variety of techniques such as X-ray crystallography (Shi, 2014) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy (Kanelis et al., 2001) have been explored for gaining insight into protein structure and function.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: NMR spectroscopy has been used to gain insight into protein structure and function.
source: Indeed, since the pioneering work of Perutz on protein crystals (Fersht, 2008), a variety of techniques such as X-ray crystallography (Shi, 2014) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy (Kanelis et al., 2001) have been explored for gaining insight into protein structure and function.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Advances in sample preparation, detector technology, and image processing have enabled atomic resolution in cryoEM studies of protein structure.
source: Advances in sample preparation, detector technology, and image processing based on single-particle analysis have also ushered in atomic resolution in cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) studies of protein structure (Nakane et al., 2020; Kühlbrandt, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Lack of specific labeling in cryoEM makes it challenging to identify small variations such as structural inhomogeneities.
source: The inherent resolution of this method is highly desirable, but lack of specific labeling makes it challenging to identify small variations such as structural inhomogeneities.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of cryoEM based on the nature of the technique.

claim: Fluorescence microscopy draws its success from exquisite specificity in labeling.
source: Fluorescence microscopy, on the other hand, draws its success from an exquisite specificity in labeling, but has traditionally suffered from a limited resolution.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of fluorescence microscopy based on established knowledge.

claim: Fluorescence microscopy has traditionally suffered from limited resolution.
source: Fluorescence microscopy, on the other hand, draws its success from an exquisite specificity in labeling, but has traditionally suffered from a limited resolution.
evidence: This is stated as a historical limitation of fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Super-resolution fluorescence microscopy has opened new avenues for studying subcellular organization.
source: The recent advent of super-resolution (SR) fluorescence microscopy has opened new avenues for studying subcellular organization and is on the way to become a workhorse for biological studies (Lelek et al., 2021; Sahl et al., 2017; Weisenburger and Sandoghdar, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Conventional SR microscopy at room temperature is not considered a contestant in structural biology for Angstrom-level information.
source: However, conventional SR microscopy performed at room temperature is still not considered as a contestant in the arena of structural biology, where Angstrom-level information about the molecular architecture of proteins and protein complexes is sought after.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of conventional SR microscopy.

claim: Performing measurements under cryogenic conditions can push the limit of fluorescence microscopy.
source: To push the limit of fluorescence microscopy, one can perform measurements under cryogenic conditions (Böning et al., 2021, Hoffman et al., 2020; Dahlberg et al., 2020; Moser et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2019; Hulleman et al., 2018b, Xu et al., 2018; Weisenburger et al., 2017; Furubayashi et al., 2017; Li et al., 2015; Weisenburger et al., 2014; Weisenburger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Cryogenic conditions slow down photochemistry, allowing each fluorophore to emit several orders of magnitude more photons than at room temperature.
source: In addition to slowing down photochemistry, which allows each fluorophore to emit several orders of magnitude more photons than at room temperature (Li et al., 2015; Weisenburger et al., 2014; Weisenburger et al., 2013), a key advantage of cryogenic temperatures is in offering superior sample preservation and high stability for Angstrom-scale structural studies.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cryogenic temperatures offer superior sample preservation and high stability for Angstrom-scale structural studies.
source: In addition to slowing down photochemistry, which allows each fluorophore to emit several orders of magnitude more photons than at room temperature (Li et al., 2015; Weisenburger et al., 2014; Weisenburger et al., 2013), a key advantage of cryogenic temperatures is in offering superior sample preservation and high stability for Angstrom-scale structural studies.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of cryogenic conditions based on established knowledge.

claim: COLD gave access to the positions of up to four labeling sites on a single protein using stochastic intensity blinking of organic dyes.
source: In one implementation, cryogenic optical localization in 3D (COLD) was introduced, where the stochastic intensity blinking of organic dyes gave access to the positions of up to four labeling sites on a single protein (Weisenburger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: A more robust protocol was employed to identify individual fluorophores by exploiting the polarization of fluorescence light dictated by fluorophore orientation.
source: We recently employed a more robust protocol to identify individual fluorophores by exploiting the polarization of the fluorescence light dictated by the fluorophore orientation (Böning et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The polarization-based method was validated by measuring single distances on one-dimensional DNA nanorulers.
source: This latter method was validated by measuring single distances on one-dimensional DNA nanorulers (Böning et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Control of fluorescence signal via polarization modulation offers an alternative to random blinking.
source: Control of the fluorescence signal via polarization modulation has also been shown to offer an alternative to random blinking (Hulleman et al., 2018a, Hafi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Distances and arrangements of protein complexes can be determined by combining images recorded from under-sampled structures.
source: Importantly, we show that the distances and arrangements of protein complexes can be determined by combining images recorded from under-sampled structures.
evidence: This is a key finding of the current study supported by experimental data.

claim: PCNA is a central functional unit in genome repair and replication.
source: Proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) is a central functional unit in genome repair and replication (Bruck and O'Donnell, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The structure of PCNA was solved by X-ray crystallography.
source: The structure of this complex protein was solved by X-ray crystallography (Georgescu et al., 2008) and more recently by cryoEM (Madru et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The structure of PCNA was solved by cryoEM.
source: The structure of this complex protein was solved by X-ray crystallography (Georgescu et al., 2008) and more recently by cryoEM (Madru et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: PCNA forms a stable homo-trimer with a pseudo-hexameric shape.
source: These studies have shown that PCNA forms a stable homo-trimer with a pseudo-hexameric shape.
evidence: This is stated based on prior structural studies.

claim: Human PCNA was fully labeled via a His-tag linker on the N-terminal side of each subunit.
source: To study human PCNA with polarCOLD, we first fully labeled it via a His-tag linker on the N-terminal side of each subunit of the protein, forming an equilateral triangle (see Materials and methods section and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: PCNA complexes were embedded in a hydrophilic poly-vinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix at sub-nanomolar concentration.
source: PCNA complexes were then embedded in a hydrophilic poly-vinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix at sub-nanomolar concentration and spin-coated on a mirror-enhanced substrate (see Böning et al., 2021 for in-depth characterization of the mirror-enhanced substrate).
evidence: This describes the sample preparation procedure.

claim: The resulting density corresponds to fewer than one protein per μm2 on average.
source: The resulting density corresponds to fewer than one protein per μm2 on average so that individual proteins can be easily identified in diffraction-limited imaging.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions achieved.

claim: A polarizing beam splitter in the detection path allows determination of the orientation of dipole-like emitters projected onto the angular interval θ ϵ [0°, 90°] in the imaging plane.
source: A polarizing beam splitter in the detection path allows us to determine the orientation of dipole-like emitters projected onto the angular interval θ ϵ [0°, 90°] in the imaging plane.
evidence: This describes the experimental setup shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The high photostability of fluorophores at T=4 K allows collection of on average 260 photons per frame (per 14 ms).
source: The high photostability of the fluorophores at T=4 K allows us to collect on average 260 photons per frame (per 14 ms) from a single fluorophore with a total number of registered photons exceeding 106 after 50,000 frames (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The total number of registered photons exceeds 106 after 50,000 frames.
source: The high photostability of the fluorophores at T=4 K allows us to collect on average 260 photons per frame (per 14 ms) from a single fluorophore with a total number of registered photons exceeding 106 after 50,000 frames (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Long photo-blinking off-times allow identification of each of the three fluorophores on a given protein complex separately.
source: The long photo-blinking off-times (Figure 1—figure supplement 2d) allow one to identify each of the three fluorophores on a given protein complex separately (Weisenburger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and a citation to prior work.

claim: An algorithm combining unsupervised statistical learning tools with change-point detection was used to fit polarization histograms.
source: To resolve the polarization histograms in cases where they partially overlap (see, e.g., Figure 1c), we fit the data using an algorithm that combines unsupervised statistical learning tools with change-point detection in a model-independent manner (White et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the analytical method used, supported by a citation.

claim: Polarization states can be robustly identified over time to assign the signal in each frame to a single fluorophore.
source: As illustrated by the red traces in Figure 1b and c, we can robustly identify the polarization states over time and hence assign the signal in each frame to a single fluorophore.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figure 1b and c.

claim: Random assignment of frames resulted in single, unresolved spots, verifying the robustness of the assignment procedure.
source: We also verified the robustness of our assignment procedure by performing random assignment of frames, which resulted in single, unresolved spots (see Materials and methods section and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a control experiment described in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The number of fluorophores that can be simultaneously resolved depends on the blinking on-off dynamics.
source: The number of fluorophores that can be simultaneously resolved depends on the blinking on-off dynamics (see Materials and methods section).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the method.

claim: Shot noise determines the angular resolution and thus the maximum number of resolvable polarization states per protein.
source: Furthermore, the shot noise determines the angular resolution and, thus, the maximum number of resolvable polarization states per protein.
evidence: This is stated as a fundamental limitation based on physics.

claim: The angular resolution directly affects the yield of resolved particles.
source: This, in turn, directly affects the yield of resolved particles (see Figure 1—figure supplements 5–6).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 5–6.

claim: With an experimental angular resolution of ca. 5°, 70% of particles containing 3 fluorophores can theoretically be resolved.
source: By taking the experimental angular resolution of ca. 5° (Figure 1—figure supplements 5–6), we can theoretically expect to resolve 70% of the particles which contain 3 fluorophores, and roughly 15% of the particles which contain 6 fluorophores.
evidence: This is based on theoretical calculations using experimental parameters.

claim: With an experimental angular resolution of ca. 5°, roughly 15% of particles containing 6 fluorophores can theoretically be resolved.
source: By taking the experimental angular resolution of ca. 5° (Figure 1—figure supplements 5–6), we can theoretically expect to resolve 70% of the particles which contain 3 fluorophores, and roughly 15% of the particles which contain 6 fluorophores.
evidence: This is based on theoretical calculations using experimental parameters.

claim: Adding a second polarization basis at a tilt of 45° would allow doubling the angular space.
source: Adding a second polarization basis at a tilt of 45°, would allow one to double the angular space (Stallinga and Rieger, 2012).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction supported by a citation.

claim: Using polarized illumination and full 3D characterization of dipole moments would result in less overlap and enhanced capacity for identifying different polarization states.
source: Moreover, using polarized illumination (Backer et al., 2016; Zhanghao et al., 2019) and a full 3D characterization of the dipole moments (Lieb et al., 2004; Mortensen et al., 2010; Hulleman et al., 2021) would result in less overlap and thus enhanced capacity for identifying different polarization states.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction supported by citations.

claim: The reconstructed fluorophore volumes agree well with the crystal structure of PCNA protein containing three identical subunits in an equilateral triangle.
source: Figure 2b shows that the reconstructed fluorophore volumes (red spheroids) agree well with the crystal structure of the PCNA protein (PDB: 1AXC) containing three identical subunits in an equilateral triangle.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The 3D reconstructed volumes correlate very well (0.96 correlation score) with the simulated accessible volumes when taking the dye linker into account.
source: Indeed, by taking the dye linker into account and calculating the accessible volume (Kalinin et al., 2012), we found that our 3D reconstructed volumes correlate very well (0.96 correlation score) with the simulated accessible volumes (see Figure 2b, Animation 1).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The Fourier shell correlation of the two half data sets gives a resolution of 4.9 Å based on the half-bit criterion.
source: The Fourier shell correlation (FSC, blue curve) of the two half data sets gives a resolution of 4.9 Å based on the half-bit criterion (red curve).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2c and represents a quantitative measure of resolution.

claim: The reconstructed side length of PCNA is 9.9±0.6 nm.
source: The model fit (red) takes the finite localization uncertainty and the random particle orientation into account, resulting in 9.9±0.6 nm.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2d and represents a quantitative measurement.

claim: The reconstructed 3D volume of PCNA was calculated from 119 particles.
source: The reconstructed 3D volume was calculated from 119 particles.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption for Figure 2.

claim: The high SNR of the method and low information density per particle deliver good results from 119 particles, which is two to three orders of magnitude lower than required for typical cryoEM measurements.
source: We note that the high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the method (see, e.g, Figure 2a), and the comparatively low information density per particle, deliver a good results from a total of 119 particles (see Figure 1—source data 2 for overall statistics), which is two to three orders of magnitude lower than the number required for typical cryoEM measurements (Cheng et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to cryoEM, supported by a citation.

claim: The low SNR in cryo-EM requires data from a large number of particles to be averaged to establish 2D classes before 3D reconstruction.
source: Indeed, the low SNR in cryo-EM requires data from a large number of particles to be first averaged to establish 2D classes before using them for 3D reconstruction (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of cryoEM, supported by a citation.

claim: In polarCOLD, each 2D projection directly contributes to the 3D reconstruction process.
source: In our case, each 2D projection directly contributes to the 3D reconstruction process.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the polarCOLD method.

claim: ClpB is a molecular machine that rescues proteins from aggregation within cells.
source: ClpB is a molecular machine that rescues proteins from aggregation within cells (Doyle et al., 2013), and its structure was shown to be very stable in the presence of ATP at low concentrations (Mazal et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The structure of ClpB was shown to be very stable in the presence of ATP at low concentrations.
source: ClpB is a molecular machine that rescues proteins from aggregation within cells (Doyle et al., 2013), and its structure was shown to be very stable in the presence of ATP at low concentrations (Mazal et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ClpB was labeled at residue S428C such that the distance between two adjacent labeling sites is expected to be 9 nm after accounting for the dye linker.
source: Here, we labeled the M-domain of the protein at residue S428C such that the distance between two adjacent labeling sites is expected to be 9 nm after accounting for the dye linker (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and expected outcome.

claim: The labeling efficiency was deliberately reduced to 50% to allow for 1/3 of the particles to carry three fluorophores.
source: We deliberately reduced the labeling efficiency to 50% in order to allow for 1/3 of the particles to carry three fluorophores as estimated by the binomial distribution (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This describes the experimental strategy based on statistical considerations.

claim: About 510 photons per frame on average were obtained from ClpB samples.
source: We obtained about 510 photons per frame on average and a significantly higher total number of photons after 100,000 frames since 87% of the molecules survived until the end of the acquisition interval (see Figure 3—figure supplement 1c-g for photo-physics charectrization).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: 87% of ClpB molecules survived until the end of the acquisition interval.
source: We obtained about 510 photons per frame on average and a significantly higher total number of photons after 100,000 frames since 87% of the molecules survived until the end of the acquisition interval (see Figure 3—figure supplement 1c-g for photo-physics charectrization).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Particles carrying three labels inherently fall into three distinct classes (I, II, and III) with multiple pair-wise distances of approximately 9, 15, and 18 nm.
source: Particles carrying three labels inherently fall into three distinct classes (I, II, and III) with multiple pair-wise distances of approximately 9, 15, and 18 nm (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is based on the geometry of the hexamer structure.

claim: A supervised classification scheme was used to assign each 2D image to one of the three classes.
source: To analyze the resulting triangle images, we used a supervised classification scheme (Gao et al., 2004) to assign each 2D image to one of the three classes, taking the angle of its plane into account.
evidence: This describes the analytical method used, supported by a citation.

claim: Template matching based on simulated ground truth images showed an accuracy of 98% in classification.
source: A control based on simulated ground truth images obtained from the crystal structure of ClpB showed an accuracy of 98% in template matching.
evidence: This is a validation of the classification method using simulated data.

claim: 232, 100, and 135 particles were obtained for classes 1, 2, and 3, respectively.
source: Overall, we obtained 232, 100, and 135 particles for classes 1, 2, and 3, respectively, representing a yield of ~7% for all the particles detected with three polarization states (see Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as the experimental outcome.

claim: The yield of classified particles represents ~7% for all particles detected with three polarization states.
source: Overall, we obtained 232, 100, and 135 particles for classes 1, 2, and 3, respectively, representing a yield of ~7% for all the particles detected with three polarization states (see Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as the experimental outcome.

claim: The reconstructed 3D volumes fit very well to the probable locations of the dye on the protein structure given by the accessible volumes.
source: Remarkably, as illustrated in Figure 3b, the reconstructed 3D volumes fit very well to the probable locations of the dye on the protein structure given by the accessible volumes (circles) on each protomer after taking the dye linker into account.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The correlation scores between the reconstructed 3D volumes and the accessible volumes of the dyes were 0.98, 0.96, and 0.86 for classes I, II, and III, respectively.
source: The correlation scores between the reconstructed 3D volumes and the accessible volumes of the dyes were 0.98, 0.96, and 0.86 for classes I, II, and III, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative measure of the agreement between experimental and theoretical data.

claim: Reconstruction of unclassified 2D images confirmed that no structure was identified.
source: As a control, we also performed a reconstruction of unclassified 2D images, and confirmed that no structure was identified (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The FSC curves suggest resolutions of 4.0, 7.9, and 6.4 Å for classes I, II, and III, respectively.
source: Again, the FSC curves of the volumes (see Figure 3—figure supplement 5a-c) suggest an exquisite resolution of 4.0, 7.9, and 6.4 Å, for classes I, II, and III, respectively.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5 and represents quantitative measures of resolution.

claim: By inspecting the raw distance histogram of unclassified particles, a peak at ~9 nm was identified as the most probable side length.
source: First, by inspecting the raw distance histogram of our unclassified particles obtained from single distance measurements (two polarization states), we could identify a peak at ~9 nm as the most probable side length of our molecules (see Figure 4a).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4a and represents an analysis of experimental data.

claim: The Akaike information criterion was used to find the best model that describes the experimental data.
source: Then, we used the Akaike information criterion (Portet, 2020; Curd et al., 2021) to find the best model that describes our experimental data (see Materials and methods section).
evidence: This describes the analytical method used, supported by citations.

claim: The hexamer structure matches the experimental data significantly better than pentamer or heptamer models.
source: As shown in Figure 4b, we found that the hexamer structure matches our data significantly better than the other models.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4b and represents a quantitative comparison.

claim: A hexamer model with reduced symmetry resulted in a considerably worse fit to the data.
source: In addition, we examined a different case of hexamer model with reduced symmetry and found that this model resulted in a considerably worse fit to our data (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4b and represents a quantitative comparison.

claim: Classification of the current data becomes less robust for deviations R>1 nm from perfect symmetry.
source: Simulations show that classification of our current data becomes less robust for R>1 nm.
evidence: This is based on simulation analysis.

claim: Solving a completely disordered structure without any prior knowledge would only be possible for complete labeling.
source: We point out that solving a completely disordered structure without any prior knowledge would only be possible for complete labeling.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the method.

claim: Existing algorithms do not provide a satisfactory solution for the data in this study.
source: As shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1, however, the existing algorithms do not provide a satisfactory solution for our data.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The failure of existing algorithms is attributed to structures being randomly oriented in 3D, strongly under-labeled, and involving similar classes.
source: We attribute this to the fact that the structures in our investigations are randomly oriented in 3D, are strongly under-labeled, and involve classes that are similar.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the observed results.

claim: polarCOLD can be extended via combination with genetic labeling.
source: polarCOLD can be further improved and extended to other modalities, for example via combination with genetic labeling (Hoffman et al., 2020; Dahlberg et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2015; Creemers et al., 2000) or by exploiting the narrow absorption and emission spectra at low temperatures for co-localization of larger numbers of fluorescent markers.
evidence: This is a prospective claim about future applications, supported by citations.

claim: polarCOLD can be extended by exploiting narrow absorption and emission spectra at low temperatures for co-localization of larger numbers of fluorescent markers.
source: polarCOLD can be further improved and extended to other modalities, for example via combination with genetic labeling (Hoffman et al., 2020; Dahlberg et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2015; Creemers et al., 2000) or by exploiting the narrow absorption and emission spectra at low temperatures for co-localization of larger numbers of fluorescent markers.
evidence: This is a prospective claim about future applications.

claim: The currently achieved SNR and Angstrom resolution of cryogenic light microscopy is capable of providing pivotal solutions for quantitative structural analysis of small proteins and large protein complexes.
source: However, the currently achieved SNR and Angstrom resolution of cryogenic light microscopy is already capable of providing pivotal solutions for quantitative structural analysis of small proteins as well as large protein complexes and aggregates.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the results of the study.

claim: An estimated 20% of the human genome encodes membrane proteins.
source: Indeed, an estimated 20% of the human genome encodes membrane proteins and many of them are potential drug targets (Piccoli et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Many membrane proteins are potential drug targets.
source: Indeed, an estimated 20% of the human genome encodes membrane proteins and many of them are potential drug targets (Piccoli et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: It is challenging to crystallize or resolve many proteins and protein complexes in their crowded surrounding.
source: The structure and active configuration of many proteins and protein complexes, however, remain out of reach because it is very challenging to crystallize or resolve them in their crowded surrounding (Cheng, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Heterogeneities caused by mobile domains and intrinsic distributions in assemblies cannot be preserved and classified robustly in EM studies, leading to smearing in final reconstruction.
source: In particular, heterogeneities caused by mobile domains and intrinsic distributions in assemblies cannot be preserved and classified in a robust fashion so that they lead to a smearing effect in the final reconstruction in EM studies (Nwanochie and Uversky, 2019; Serna, 2019; Scheres, 2016; Scheres et al., 2007, Orlova and Saibil, 2004; Papai et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: A future direction is to vitrify biological samples via rapid freezing or high-pressure freezing to exploit polarCOLD for identifying particles in low-contrast EM micrographs.
source: A future direction is, thus, to vitrify biological samples via rapid freezing (Dubochet and McDowall, 1981) or high-pressure freezing (Studer et al., 2008; Hoffman et al., 2020) in order to exploit the high spatial resolution, sensitivity and specificity of polarCOLD for identifying and determining the positions and orientations of individual particles of interest in low-contrast EM micrographs.
evidence: This is a prospective claim about future applications, supported by citations.

claim: The combination of cryogenic light microscopy with cryoEM has attracted attention for cellular and tissue imaging.
source: The combination of cryogenic light microscopy with cryoEM has attracted attention for cellular and tissue imaging, although the existing reports do not surpass a resolution of about 10 nm (Dahlberg and Moerner, 2021; Hoffman et al., 2020; Dahlberg et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2020; Tuijtel et al., 2019; Wolff et al., 2016; de Boer et al., 2015; Loussert Fonta and Humbel, 2015; Kaufmann et al., 2014b, Chang et al., 2014; Kaufmann et al., 2014a, Faas et al., 2013; Watanabe et al., 2011; Mironov and Beznoussenko, 2009; Agronskaia et al., 2008; Sartori et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Existing reports of combined cryogenic light microscopy and cryoEM do not surpass a resolution of about 10 nm.
source: The combination of cryogenic light microscopy with cryoEM has attracted attention for cellular and tissue imaging, although the existing reports do not surpass a resolution of about 10 nm (Dahlberg and Moerner, 2021; Hoffman et al., 2020; Dahlberg et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2020; Tuijtel et al., 2019; Wolff et al., 2016; de Boer et al., 2015; Loussert Fonta and Humbel, 2015; Kaufmann et al., 2014b, Chang et al., 2014; Kaufmann et al., 2014a, Faas et al., 2013; Watanabe et al., 2011; Mironov and Beznoussenko, 2009; Agronskaia et al., 2008; Sartori et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing work, supported by citations.

claim: The median registration error is less than 2 nm.
source: Registered PSFs are grouped and their polarization is calculated from the intensities. Single fluorophores are identified via this feature and used as fiducial markers to perform additional drift correction and establish a more precise image alignment via an interpolated map. The residual drift is well below 1 nm and the median registration error is less than 2 nm.
evidence: This is a quantitative measure of the image analysis quality.
